answer: The captain signs each watchman onto the roster every night, and the roster is read at dawn to prove the camp was guarded. A copper watchman who slept through his watch fails the roster: at the ripple of the night his name must stand beside the hour he actually kept, and a sleeping name is written in another hand. Buying a false roster means bribing the captain, forging ninety nights and paying 12,200, while the jetty signature on the roster is checked by the caravan master, so a watchman whose nights were never kept is left behind at the well.
